gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named reviewer's measured 10GbE throughput for the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus with hard drives. Mighty Gadget measured 500–600 MB/s from a RAID 5 array of WD Red Plus drives, and named the drives, not the 10GbE link, as the limit. That is about twice the roughly 290 MB/s Club386 measured on a 2.5GbE NAS (QNAP TS-464), and below the 670 MB/s ChatGPT assumed for 10GbE.
standout_why: Compared against Fstoppers (cited, 2026-10-28) and Camera Lookout (cited, 2026-09-23). Fstoppers gives no measured figures for any of the candidates: its only test is a TerraMaster F2-425 Plus copy (35.5 GB in about nine minutes), and the rest are maker claims. Camera Lookout says it did not test anything. Its only measurement for a candidate is Club386's QNAP TS-464 result (a little over 290 MB/s, about 55 W active and 19 W standby). For the DXP4800 Plus and DS925+ it gives only maker figures (UGREEN 42.36 W / 18.12 W, Synology 522/565 MB/s and 37.91 W). No rival or top result gives a measured 10GbE hard-drive throughput for the DXP4800 Plus, or a measured idle and load wattage for the DS925+. The Adobe pages and the needtoknowit guide give no measurements.
decides: Confirms the DXP4800 Plus as the speed pick but corrects how much faster it is. With hard drives, 10GbE gives about 2× the 2.5GbE models (500–600 vs about 290 MB/s), not the 4× the port speeds suggest. Copying 100 GB of RAW files takes about 3.0 minutes instead of about 5.7. The gap matters for big imports and for building previews, not for editing one file. A shopper who edits locally and archives to the NAS loses little with the DS925+ or TS-464. On power, the measured figures are close: CGMagazine measured the DS925+ at up to 28 W idle and 62–64 W at full load, and Mighty Gadget measured the DXP4800 Plus at 39–45 W under light load and 64 W at peak.

findings.label: Measured 10GbE transfer speed from a hard-drive array (Mighty Gadget, James Smythe)
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800 Plus Review – Is this the best 10GbE NAS for a Media Server? (Mighty Gadget, 2025-11-14, updated 2026-04-01)
findings.note: RAID 5 of WD Red Plus hard drives, over 10GbE. The reviewer names the drives, not the network, as the limit. The drive count and capacity, the client and the test tool are not stated. Arithmetic: 100,000 MB ÷ 550 MB/s ≈ 182 s ≈ 3.0 min, vs ≈ 5.7 min at 290 MB/s.

findings.label: Measured power draw at the wall (Mighty Gadget)
findings.value: 39–45 W light load (photo transfer); about 47 W during 4K playback; about 32 W in the evening; 64 W peak
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800 Plus Review (Mighty Gadget)
findings.note: The reviewer links the 64 W peak to switching two M.2 SSDs to read/write cache. Mighty Gadget estimates about £84 a year at about 24p/kWh, from a 40 W average.

findings.label: Synthetic workload traces, 10GbE vs 2.5GbE (KitGuru, Simon Crisp)
findings.value: File Server: 1,166.25 MB/s (10GbE) vs 330.25 MB/s (2.5GbE). Workstation: 162 vs 178.5 MB/s
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus 4-bay NAS review, p. 11 (KitGuru, 2024-05-28)
findings.note: File Server trace: 512 MB file, 16 KB blocks, 80% read, 100% random, queue depth 128. Workstation trace: 8K transfers, 80% read, 80% random. The page does not name the drives or RAID level. A 1.1 GB/s random rate suggests the data came from cache, so this is not a hard-drive sequential figure. The Workstation result shows no 10GbE advantage on small random I/O.

findings.label: Measured power draw (CGMagazine, Brendan Frye)
findings.value: Up to 28 W idle; 62–64 W at full load
findings.note: Four drives, both 2.5GbE ports active at full load. Drive models are not named. Temperatures were 34–39 °C under continuous access. The review's 522/565 MB/s 'testing' figures equal Synology's rated numbers, so they are left out as a likely repeat of the spec sheet.

findings.label: Measured 2.5GbE throughput and power (Club386, quoted by Camera Lookout)
findings.value: A little over 290 MB/s on 2.5GbE; about 55 W active with four drives; about 19 W in standby
findings.source_title: Best NAS systems for photographers in 2026 (Camera Lookout, 2026-09-23)
findings.note: Second-hand: the Club386 original was not opened. A secondary search summary says four 8 TB IronWolf drives in RAID 10. This figure is already on a cited rival page, so it is a baseline for 2.5GbE, not new to the page.

unsourced: An independent measured single-link 2.5GbE throughput for the Synology DS925+: Techarp (reported 295 MB/s read and 310 MB/s write in search snippets) and Neowin (250–300 MB/s) both returned 403. Macworld, Exhibit Tech, Smartprix, iFeelTech and Willie Howe only repeat Synology's 522/565 MB/s.
TechPowerUp's DXP4800 Plus power measurements (about 67 W average in RAID 5 under 10GbE load, under about 26 W with drives asleep, per snippet): the page returned 403 twice.
Club386's original TS-464 review and Digital Citizen's TS-464 review: the Club386 page did not come up in search, and Digital Citizen returned 403.

A timed Lightroom Classic test (import, preview build or catalog browse) of RAW files on a NAS over 10GbE vs 2.5GbE vs local SSD: no named reviewer or lab found. Puget Bench times imports on a single system only. frameandfocal's 8.7 s vs 0.9 s catalog-open figures have no traceable source.
Measured noise in dB(A) for the DXP4800 Plus, DS925+ and TS-464: none of the reviews I opened gives one. NASCompares' reported 36–37 dB(A) for the DS925+ appeared only in a search summary.
Measurements for the UGREEN DXP4800 Pro and DXP4800 GT: not researched because of the tool-call budget.
